prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “AI visibility” service that reliably tells you whether ChatGPT (and other LLM-powered assistants) will recommend your business. The best practical approach is a combination: (A) use a knowledge-distribution/listing service to make sure authoritative sources have correct info, and (B) monitor LLMs directly (manually or via automated queries) plus track local-search signals. Top tools and steps:

1) Use a knowledge-distribution / listings service (best single commercial pick)
- Yext — purpose-built to push your official business data (hours, services, descriptions, attributes) to many platforms and to power AI/assistant integrations. It’s the most direct way to make your business part of the knowledge bases many AIs draw on.

2) Monitor local search & citations
- BrightLocal, Whitespark, Local Falcon, or Moz Local — track rankings, citations, and local-pack visibility across Google, Bing, Yelp, etc. These show the real-world signals assistants use.

3) Track big platforms’ data
- Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp — claim/manage listings and use their analytics. These are primary sources behind many assistant responses.

4) Check LLMs directly (recommended for actual validation)
- Manually query ChatGPT, Bing Chat, Google Bard and voice assistants with realistic prompts (“Recommend a [service] near [your neighborhood]”, “Where can I find [specific service] in [city]?”). Try variations of wording and common user intents.
- Automate if you want regular checks: use the OpenAI API (for ChatGPT-like responses), Bing Web Search / Chat APIs, and Bard API to run a battery of prompts and log responses. Flag any mentions of your business.

5) Improve your chance of being recommended
- Add structured data/schema.org to your website (LocalBusiness markup), maintain consistent NAP (name/address/phone), gather reviews, and build local backlinks. Good on-site SEO and authoritative citations increases the chance LLMs cite you or rank you highly in the sources they summarize.

6) Consider specialist reputation/local SEO monitoring vendors
- Chatmeter and Podium (reviews/reputation + local listings) or an SEO agency that offers “AI visibility” monitoring if you want a hands-off solution.

Example prompts to test ChatGPT/Bard/Bing:
- “Recommend three HVAC companies in [city, zip] with good reviews and prices.”
- “Where can I get [service X] near [landmark or neighborhood]?”
- “What are top-rated [service] providers in [city]?”

Important caveats
- LLMs don’t always “cite” the source that led them to a recommendation, and outputs can vary by model, prompt, date, and whether the assistant uses browsing or knowledge connectors.
- Ensuring strong, consistent presence on authoritative platforms (Google, Yelp, Apple, and a knowledge-distribution vendor like Yext) is the most reliable way to influence whether AI engines surface your business.

If you want, tell me your city and business category and I can:
- Suggest a short set of test prompts for automation, and
- Draft the exact structured-data snippet and listing checklist you should publish to maximize AI visibility.
